plain_summary: Check for a full blood count in the past year during stable carbamazepine or valproate treatment.

medicine_groups.name: Carbamazepine or valproate
medicine_groups.note: Count oral valproate recorded as valproic acid or by its salt, including oral tablets, liquid and syrup. The listed Epilim products contain sodium valproate.

needs_facts.what: Timing of full blood count at the latest stable carbamazepine or valproate supply
needs_facts.meets: At the latest qualifying supply, check dated full blood count, including tests done elsewhere, against the previous 12 calendar months and any shorter documented plan. Count the boundary date as in time. A pharmacist who has checked the test date may confirm its timing against both checks. Use the date the sample was taken, including for a count done elsewhere. A confirmed sample date is enough to check timing even if the test values are unavailable. The date the answer was entered does not establish the sample date. A missing or overdue test supports only a possible gap. If the date or timing is uncertain, keep the gap unconfirmed.

options.words: Done within 12 calendar months and in time under any shorter documented plan
The latest test was more than 12 calendar months earlier
Within 12 calendar months but overdue under a shorter documented plan
No completed test was found after checking for tests done elsewhere

needs_facts.what: Individual follow-up plan for full blood count
needs_facts.meets: At the latest qualifying supply, check whether a shorter deadline in the individual plan has passed without the requested test. A confirmed missed deadline gives a possible gap. If there is no outstanding earlier test, the annual check still applies. If a shorter plan is known but its timing or completion is unclear, ask for the due date and the latest test date.

options.words: An earlier deadline has passed without the test
The earlier test was completed or is not yet due
There is no shorter testing plan

rule_for_models: At the latest qualifying supply, use refill dates, quantities and daily directions to check for at least 12 months of ongoing stable carbamazepine or oral valproate treatment, excluding a completed switch or an incomplete treatment window. Use the sample date, including for a count done elsewhere. A pharmacist who has checked that date may confirm whether the annual check and any shorter deadline were met. Report no finding if the latest full blood count is within the previous 12 calendar months (including the boundary) and meets any shorter documented plan. If the count is missing, overdue or undated, or the timing of a known shorter plan is unclear, report only a possible full blood count gap, cite the supplies and any result or plan, and ask for the test date and any earlier deadline, checking daily dose, interruptions and current use if continuity is unclear so the pharmacist can judge borderline gaps.
cannot_be_seen: Outside pathology or follow-up may be missing. An incomplete observation window cannot establish an overdue test.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the date of the last full blood count during ongoing carbamazepine or valproate treatment and when the next count is due under the annual or individual plan?
